statement: In adults who smoked cigarettes and joined randomised trials of nicotine vapes (Cochrane living review, searched to 1 January 2026; follow-up from 1 week to about 2 years), the evidence is insufficient to say whether a nicotine vape, compared with nicotine replacement or with a vape without nicotine, changes the risk of serious or other adverse events: no clear difference was seen, but events were few. Serious adverse events: 7 against 6 in 100 with a vape against nicotine replacement (risk difference 0.01, 95% CI −0.01 to 0.02; 10 trials, 4,045 people; moderate certainty) and 2 against 2 in 100 against a vape without nicotine (0.00, −0.01 to 0.01; 11 trials, 1,786 people; low certainty, fewer than 100 events). Any adverse event: 39 against 41 in 100 against nicotine replacement (risk ratio 0.95, 0.72 to 1.24; 8 trials, 3,107 people; low certainty; I² 72%) and 46 against 46 in 100 against a vape without nicotine (1.01, 0.95 to 1.08; 6 trials, 909 people; moderate certainty). Against behavioural support only or no support the certainty is very low: serious events 3 against 3 in 100 (0.00, −0.00 to 0.01; 18 trials, 5,032 people; 10 of the 18 trials recorded none) and any adverse event 52 against 43 in 100 (risk ratio 1.22, 1.00 to 1.49, an interval that touches no difference; 11 trials, 2,801 people). No trial in the comparisons with nicotine replacement had tobacco or vaping industry funding; one or two trials in each of the other two comparisons did, and leaving them out did not change the review's reading of any of these results (for any adverse event against support only or no support the risk ratio then read 1.26, 0.96 to 1.66). Trials that could not be pooled reported more throat or mouth irritation, cough or dry mouth with vapes in some trials and fewer breathing symptoms in others, and more nausea with nicotine replacement in one. The trials used regulated nicotine vapes in adults for up to about 2 years; the review says longer-term effects are unknown, that its conclusion relates to people using regulated vapes to stop smoking and not to people who have never smoked, and that products containing cannabis or illicit products may have different harm profiles. Certainty: low (for the comparisons with nicotine replacement and with a vape without nicotine; very low against support only or no support). Status: replicated.
plain: In these trials, serious health problems were about as common in people given a nicotine vape as in people given nicotine patches, gum or similar (about 7 in 100 against 6 in 100) or a vape without nicotine (about 2 in 100 in both). Side effects of any kind were also about as common with those two comparisons. Against counselling only or nothing the evidence is weaker, and the vape groups reported somewhat more side effects (about 52 in 100 against 43 in 100, though the range includes no difference). None of the trials against patches, gum or similar was paid for by the vaping or tobacco industry; one or two in each of the other comparisons were, and the review found that leaving them out did not change its reading. The trials were too small and too short (up to about 2 years) to show rare or later harms.
population: Adults who smoked cigarettes and joined randomised trials of nicotine vapes; adverse events 8, 6 and 11 trials (3,107, 909 and 2,801 people) and serious adverse events 10, 11 and 18 trials (4,045, 1,786 and 5,032 people) against nicotine replacement, vapes without nicotine, and support only or no support; follow-up 1 week to about 2 years; Cochrane living review, search to 1 January 2026
comparator: Nicotine replacement therapy; a vape without nicotine; behavioural support only or no support
outcome: Any adverse event and serious adverse event during follow-up of one week or longer (self-report and medical records)
magnitude: Serious adverse events (risk difference; per 100 with comparator vs vape): vs NRT 0.01 (−0.01 to 0.02), 6 vs 7 (5–8), 10 trials, 4,045 participants, moderate; vs non-nicotine vape 0.00 (−0.01 to 0.01), 2 vs 2 (1–3), 11 trials, 1,786, low; vs behavioural support only or no support 0.00 (−0.00 to 0.01), 3 vs 3 (3–4), 18 trials, 5,032, very low. Any adverse event (RR): vs NRT 0.95 (0.72–1.24), 41 vs 39 per 100 (30–51), 8 trials, 3,107, I² 72%, low; vs non-nicotine vape 1.01 (0.95–1.08), 46 vs 46 per 100 (44–50), 6 trials, 909, moderate; vs support only or no support 1.22 (1.00–1.49), 43 vs 52 per 100 (43–64), 11 trials, 2,801, I² 58%, very low. Industry-funded trials left out (Table 2): none to remove against NRT; against a vape without nicotine any adverse event 1.01 (0.95–1.08) and serious events −0.00 (−0.01 to 0.01), unchanged; against support only or no support the review reports no change in reading for serious events, and any adverse event reads 1.26 (0.96–1.66), I² 60%.

evidence.locator: Results › Synthesis of results › Adverse events, 1st paragraph and Sensitivity analyses; Serious adverse events, 1st and 2nd paragraphs; Narrative summary of unpooled studies; Summary of findings 1
evidence.extracted: Nicotine vape against NRT: any adverse event RR 0.95 (0.72 to 1.24), I² 72%, 8 trials, 3,107 participants, 41 per 100 with NRT against 39 per 100 (30 to 51) with the vape, low certainty (imprecision and inconsistency). Serious events RD 0.01 (−0.01 to 0.02), I² 0%, 10 trials, 4,045, 6 per 100 against 7 per 100 (5 to 8), moderate certainty (fewer than 300 events). No trial in either pool was industry-funded. Unpooled: Hajek 2019 found nausea more often with NRT and throat or mouth irritation more often with the vape.

evidence.locator: Results › Synthesis of results › Adverse events › Versus non-nicotine; Serious adverse events › Versus non-nicotine EC; Summary of findings 2; Table 2 (Analyses 8.2 and 8.3)
evidence.extracted: Nicotine against non-nicotine vape: any adverse event RR 1.01 (0.95 to 1.08), I² 0%, 6 trials, 909 participants, 46 against 46 per 100 (44 to 50), moderate certainty (imprecision). Serious events RD 0.00 (−0.01 to 0.01), I² 0%, 11 trials, 1,786, 2 against 2 per 100 (1 to 3), low certainty (fewer than 100 events, two levels); five of 12 trials reporting serious events had none. Two unpooled trials found similar adverse event rates, two reported more events with the nicotine vape. Industry funding: one trial in the any-adverse-event pool and two (Caponnetto 2013, Rose 2023) in the serious-event pool; removing them made no change to either result (Table 2: RR 1.01, 0.95 to 1.08; RD −0.00, −0.01 to 0.01).

evidence.locator: Results › Synthesis of results › Adverse events › Versus behavioural support or no support; Narrative summary of unpooled studies; Serious adverse events › Versus behavioural support or no support; Summary of findings 3; Table 2 (Analysis 9.2)
evidence.extracted: Nicotine vape against behavioural support only or no support: any adverse event RR 1.22 (1.00 to 1.49), I² 58%, 11 trials, 2,801 participants, 43 per 100 with behavioural support or no support against 52 per 100 (43 to 64) with the vape, very low certainty (risk of bias and imprecision). Serious events RD 0.00 (−0.00 to 0.01), I² 0%, 18 trials, 5,032, 3 against 3 per 100 (3 to 4), very low certainty; ten of 18 trials reported none. Seven further trials compared the vape with behavioural support only or traditional cigarettes and gave adverse event data that could not be pooled, with mixed direction by symptom (against traditional cigarettes, more throat irritation, cough and dry mouth in one trial and fewer respiratory symptoms in another). Industry support: one trial (Cravo 2016) in the any-adverse-event pool and two (Edmiston 2022, Cravo 2016) in the serious-event pool; the review says removing them did not affect interpretation (Table 2 gives RR 1.26, 0.96 to 1.66, I² 60%, for any adverse event without the industry-supported trial).

evidence.extracted: Authors: longer-term health effects are unknown and the review includes safety data to two years only; the trials tested regulated nicotine vapes and illicit products or products containing other active substances such as THC may have different harm profiles; imprecision remains the main limit for some comparisons; unpublished data may be missing.

imprecision.note: Serious events against vapes without nicotine: fewer than 100 events (two levels in the review); against nicotine replacement fewer than 300 events, and any adverse event against NRT: imprecision and I² 72%.

grade.reasoning: Randomised evidence, starting high; the rating is for the comparisons with nicotine replacement and with vapes without nicotine, and the comparison with support only or no support, which the review rates very low, is labelled in the statement rather than allowed to set the claim's rating (METHODS §6.3; the same approach as the all-cause estimate in the methamphetamine mortality claim). Imprecision, two levels: serious adverse events against vapes without nicotine rest on fewer than 100 events (the review's two levels); against nicotine replacement the review took one level for fewer than 300 events, and for any adverse event against nicotine replacement one level for imprecision and one for inconsistency (I² 72%); all reach low. Risk of bias, not rated down for these two comparisons (the review does not downgrade them; for support only or no support it takes levels for unblinded assessment and differential contact). Indirectness, not rated down: regulated vapes supplied in trials, adults, up to about 2 years. Relation insufficient-evidence because the intervals do not exclude a difference of about 2 serious events in 100 against nicotine replacement and the trials were too short and too small to show rare or later harms (METHODS §6.3: no detectable effect needs an interval that excludes meaningful effects). Status replicated for the main finding, serious events, whose pools have I² 0% in all three comparisons; adverse events overall are less consistent (I² 72% and 58%), which the statement shows. Living review: later updates will change the numbers.

verification.flag_note: Staged apart from the quitting claims because harms carry lower ratings. Certainty follows Cochrane's ratings for each comparison; the claim-level rating is set by the two comparisons with another product (low), with the comparison against support only or no support (very low) labelled in the statement, as in the methamphetamine mortality model. Relation insufficient-evidence is a cautious choice (see the grade reasoning); the senior author may prefer does-not-detectably-change for serious events against nicotine replacement (moderate certainty). Not covered here, by design: exposure to chemicals and long-term disease (other readers' claims); biomarkers and lung function in these trials (on the card). Not read: supplementary materials, the unpooled trials' own reports.
